You are working in the Go repository at /gin (gin web framework). No internet. Do not look at any gin copy outside /gin. Only edit /gin/tree.go (plus a temporary test file you create and delete).

BUG to fix in /gin/tree.go, function `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` (around line 700-860).

Current structure: inside the `walk:` loop, after the "Add common prefix to result" part, the code has a block `if !n.wildChild { ... }` which (a) skips already-processed rune bytes and looks up the next child by matching `n.indices` (recursing for a new rune, trying the lowercase then the uppercase form), and (b) if nothing matched, returns nil (or applies the fixTrailingSlash rule). After that block the code unconditionally does:

		n = n.children[0]
		switch n.nType {
		case param:

This is wrong: the wildcard child is always the LAST element of `n.children` (see `addChild`), so when a node has both static children and a wildcard child, `n.children[0]` is a static node with nType 0 and the `switch` falls into `default: panic("invalid node type")`. Even when it does not panic, the static children are never tried, so `findCaseInsensitivePath` cannot find the case-corrected static route (e.g. routes "/x" and "/:cc": looking up "/X" must return "/x").

REQUIRED FIX: restructure so that the index/rune lookup is always attempted first, and the wildcard child is only used as a fallback. Concretely, move the body of the `if !n.wildChild { ... }` block (the `rb = shiftNRuneBytes(rb, npLen)` part, the `if rb[0] != 0 { ... } else { ... }` part) OUT of the `if`, so it always runs; keep the "Nothing found. We can recommend to redirect to the same URL without a trailing slash if a leaf exists for that path" part (`if fixTrailingSlash && path == "/" && n.handlers != nil { return ciPath }` / `return nil`) inside `if !n.wildChild { ... }`; and then replace `n = n.children[0]` with the wildcard child, i.e.

		// Handle wildcard child, which is always at the end of the array
		n = n.children[len(n.children)-1]
		switch n.nType {

Keep the rest of the function (the param and catchAll cases, the `default: panic("invalid node type")`) unchanged. Do not change any other function.

VERIFICATION (run and report verbatim):
1. cd /gin && gofmt -l tree.go (must print nothing)
2. cd /gin && go build ./... && go vet ./... 2>&1 | tail -20
3. cd /gin && go test -run 'TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePath' -v . 2>&1 | tail -40 (must PASS)
4. Create a TEMPORARY test file /gin/zz_tmp_tree_test.go in package gin with:

package gin

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestTmpFindCaseInsensitiveMultipleChildrenAndWildcard(t *testing.T) {
	tree := &node{}
	for _, route := range []string{"/x", "/:cc", "/cmd/whoami", "/cmd/:tool/"} {
		tree.addRoute(route, fakeHandler(route))
	}

	out, found := tree.findCaseInsensitivePath("/X", false)
	assert.True(t, found)
	assert.Equal(t, "/x", string(out))

	out, found = tree.findCaseInsensitivePath("/CMD/WHOAMI", false)
	assert.True(t, found)
	assert.Equal(t, "/cmd/whoami", string(out))

	out, found = tree.findCaseInsensitivePath("/CMD/TOOL", true)
	assert.True(t, found)
	assert.Equal(t, "/cmd/TOOL/", string(out))
}

Run: cd /gin && go test -run 'TestTmpFindCaseInsensitive' -v . 2>&1 | tail -40 (must PASS; if an assertion fails, report the actual value verbatim).
5. DELETE /gin/zz_tmp_tree_test.go (rm -f) and confirm it is gone.
6. Run the FULL suite: cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -30. Report any failure verbatim. If your change broke a previously passing test, revert to the original code (`git checkout -- tree.go`) and report that instead.

Report: `git diff tree.go`, verbatim output of each step, PASS/FAIL per step, and the exact result of step 4 (including actual values if it failed).

GOAL: find the bug in /gin/tree.go that makes a test named `TestRouteParamsNotEmpty` fail. That test is NOT in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour: for a matched route that contains URL parameters, the params must not be empty. The bug is a small deviation from correct code in tree.go (an injected bug), so look for code that is subtly wrong rather than missing features.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Read /gin/tree.go completely and study: `Params.Get`/`ByName`, `countParams`, `findWildcard`, `insertChild`, `addRoute`, `getValue` (especially the param case around line 490-520, the catchAll case around line 540-570, the skippedNodes rollback code, and the `if params != nil && cap(*params) > 0` guard).
2. Empirically test the behaviour. Write a TEMPORARY test file /gin/zz_tmp_params_test.go (package gin) that exercises many route/request combinations through BOTH `node.getValue` and a real `New()` router + httptest, asserting that `c.Params` is non-empty and has the right key/values for routes with :params and *catchAll, e.g. routes "/:a", "/:a/:b", "/x/:a", "/x/:a/*b", "/:a/x", "/cmd/:tool/:sub", "/src/*filepath", "/user_:name", "/files/:dir/*filepath", and requests like "/1", "/1/2", "/x/1", "/x/1/2/3", "/cmd/a/b", "/src/some/file.png", "/user_gopher", "/files/js/inc/framework.js". Also test with `params := make(Params, 0)` (zero capacity) and with `make(Params, 0, 10)`. Report every case where the result differs from what the route pattern implies (missing param, empty value, wrong key, extra param, panic).
3. Also run the existing suites: `cd /gin && go test -run 'TestTree|TestRoute' -v . 2>&1 | tail -60` and `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -20` and report the results.
4. If (and only if) you find a case where a matched route's params are missing/empty/wrong because of a small code deviation, fix it minimally in /gin/tree.go, then re-run: `gofmt -l tree.go`, `go build ./... && go vet ./...`, your temporary test, and the FULL suite `go test ./...`. The full suite MUST stay green (the baseline is green); if any pre-existing test fails, revert your change (`git checkout -- tree.go`) and report the failure instead.
5. DELETE every temporary test file you created (rm -f /gin/zz_tmp_params_test.go) and confirm they are gone with ls.

Report: (a) the list of tested cases and their actual results, (b) any anomaly found with the exact line of tree.go responsible, (c) the `git diff tree.go` if you changed it, (d) verbatim test output for every command you ran, (e) a clear statement of whether you changed tree.go or not.
